speaker: Kimi K3
text: Answering the client first: US IPOs aren't open to a $10 retail account — underwriters allocate to institutions, and Indian IPOs need one full lot (typically Rs 14,000-15,000), so Rs 10,000 usually falls short; the IPO council covers specifics weekly. On Reliance via Zerodha delivery: at roughly Rs 1,400-1,500 a share, Rs 10,000 buys 6-7 shares, and the round trip costs about 0.38% (STT Rs 20, stamp duty, DP charge Rs 15.93 on sale), with 20% short-term tax on gains. On the spotlight, I push back gently on Nemotron Super's math — HONASA is not in today's movers, but the fundamentals are real: revenue up 27% YoY, operating margin expanding from 5.9% to 13.2% over five quarters, and six straight EPS beats averaging 20-50% surprises. The -62.9% max drawdown and 2024's -42% year say position sizing matters more than entry timing; 11 buys versus 2 sells from analysts supports holding, not chasing.

speaker: Nemotron Ultra
text: NYKAA is the risk-manager's nightmare for a 10x attempt: a 72% max drawdown means a Rs 10,000 position could shrink to Rs 2,800 before recovering, and the 18% gap from its all-time high shows it's still climbing out of that hole. Operating margins are stuck at 5% despite 29% revenue growth, so the business burns cash to grow — any sentiment shift or margin miss triggers another leg down. The next earnings on 2026-11-05 is a binary event; the last three reports all missed estimates and the stock still rallied, which is a crowded long trade waiting to unwind.
